title: MV Dea (v1.0.0) - A self-proclaimed goddess, a boy and a universe full of mysteries

posts.author: jose3003
posts.body:
My first game, Dea, is now available on Steam!
I worked on this game for some years during my free time in RPGMaker MV, and it's finally released!
This RPG takes place in a future world, or what's left of it after a war that razed most of it, where people keep on with their lives. One of them is Hikuro, a boy that's suddenly called by someone who says to be a goddess, Dea. This goddess will ask Hikuro and his friends to protect their world from a plague of monsters that turn corpses into more of their kind, but it seems there's more to it...
This game is inspired by classic RPGs: turn-based battles, creating equipment with the materials monsters drop, side quests, magic and special abilities... All those things we love so much!
But the biggest selling point of Dea is its universe: charismatic characters and their stories, conversations where even the slightest details can hide a deeper meaning, a universe full of mysteries... Exploration in this game is usually rewarded with good equipment, lore or even both.
Dea is available on Steam by 14.99€ (13.31€ during the first week), and you can play it in English or Spanish.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Just a couple more things since I already gave you my feedback in a PM.
First, don't get discouraged. I think you are going to find that the critics both here and on Steam can be pretty candid and, as I mentioned privately, your game does have some hot spots that typically generate negative comments. I wouldn't be surprised if some Steam users buy the game just so they can play like .2 hours and then leave a negative review. Heck, there are some Steam users who will negative bomb any RPG Maker game they find, no matter how good it is.

Anyway, don't get discouraged. All feedback is worth considering. Congrats on what you have accomplished and good luck!

posts.author: Dalph
posts.body:
@ZombieKidzRule
The biggest issue is the price here, it's insanely high for the effort put there, if it was a free game, nobody would've said much.
This game costs more than OneShot, which is a fantastic RPG Maker game.
It's not true that Steam users hate on every RPG Maker game out there just because, they usually downvote only RTP asset flips\low effort RPG Maker games.
If a lot of effort is put, then they have no problems with the games, just look at Omori, OneShot, To the Moon franchise, Lisa, Yume Nikki, Fear & Hunger, Rakuen, Mr. Saitou, Jimmy and the Pulsating Mass, and a few others I can't recall...these games are all made with RPG Maker (Steam players are aware of it) and yet have excellent reviews on Steam.
This is clearly their first ever RPG Maker project and IMHO, it was a big mistake to make it commercial, the dev should've known what's coming for them if they didn't practice enough with the engine.
I made 3 small free games (mostly by myself) in the past before even thinking about going commercial, and tbh I'm still not confident about it.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule

@Dalph
I just want to re-emphasize my use of the words "
some Steam users
" because that has been my experience with reading through many reviews on Steam. I am sure that some very popular RPG Maker games on Steam don't experience that, but I have also seen a far amount of RPG Maker games on Steam where there are negative reviews about it being shovel ware and the same old RTP assets when that isn't even remotely true, just from looking at the screenshots and watching the clips. It makes me wonder if the person making the review has even seen the RTP assets or if they are just making assumptions. If you haven't seen reviews like that, I guess that is fortunate for you because, honestly, those types of reviews sort of tick me off and they stick in my, admittedly, bad memory.
So no, just to clarify in case my previous post wasn't worded correctly, I don't think I insinuated that Steam users hate on every RPG Maker game because that certainly isn't true. But I do think that
some Steam users
do have an automatic negative impression of RPG Maker games, in general, and that can show in the reviews they leave after playing for 15-30 minutes before reviewing and refunding.

posts.author: Dalph
posts.body:
@ZombieKidzRule
There will always be *a few* people downvoting things just because (haters), and that happens to every media, it's impossible to completely please the masses, and the engine sadly has a bad reputation already. I'm not sure which non RTP games you are talking about here, but I can tell you that RPG Maker has a very distinctive look and it's easily recognizable.
If you have a custom resource pack and then you use the balloonhead RTP sprites with it, people will still bash on your commercial game saying *asset flip*, because it has some RTP elements and still looks too much like default RPG Maker.
The same happens if you use the default UI/menu.
It's the little things many devs usually don't edit at all (SE too!) that give to their games that default RPG Maker look, not just the graphics.
RTP shouldn't be used at all for commercial games though, the more they use it, the more the engine's reputation gets tarnished.

posts.author: brandonjadams
posts.body:
Unfortunately, everyone is going to know these are RTP assets, including those outside the RPGMaker community, because this engine is notorious for the thousands of games made with these assets and tossed onto Steam for excessive prices. You may have seen a few $14.99 games at the top of the Steam pile for RPGMaker (and quite a few less than that), but if you start scrolling down you'll see far, far more such games with negative or no reviews. The titles at the top are the exception, and they've got a lot in their games that Dea currently does not, including a lot of engine modifications.
A strong story is good but not sufficient to make up for lack in other areas. To really stick out with this engine, you really need an original art approach (or at the very least an asset pack used coherently and interestingly), top-notch mapmaking, fresh mechanics, and flawless execution in pretty much everything. I'm trying it myself and even I know full well I'm on an uphill slope.
You're on the way, man. You're just not quite as far along as you thought you were.
